newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch banker warns of "paper" EMU deficit cuts.
newsitem.headline: Dutch banker warns of "paper" EMU deficit cuts.

text.p: The next president of the Dutch central bank said on Tuesday EU member states must not be tempted to make "paper" reductions in their deficits and debts in order to qualify for European economic and monetary union.

Arnout Wellink, who will succeed Wim Duisenberg as head of the central bank in June, said much work remained to be done in the area of public finances as a "clear majority" of EU states did not yet fulfil the EMU budgetary criteria.

"Tempting as they may be, all sorts of mere 'paper' reductions in deficits and debts should be rigorously avoided, and only budgetary cuts that conform to statistical conventions and make economic sense should be allowed," he said.

Wellink, currently an executive director of the Dutch central bank, made his remarks in a speech at a conference organised by the Finnish embassy in the Netherlands. A text of his speech was distributed to news media in advance.
Wellink said the convergence criteria had to be taken seriously in order for EMU participants to benefit fully from the advantages of monetary union.
"Only if EMU proves its soundness, and the euro becomes a stable currency, at least as stable as the Dutch guilder and the German mark, will the benefits materialise in full," he said.
He said a weak euro and high interest rates, would not be in the interest of those countries with stable economies.

Furthermore, countries which did not meet strictly applied convergence criteria would not benefit from early entry into EMU as they would no longer be able to lower their interest rates to counter the effects of a sudden economic recession, he said.

Wellink said he was confident the Netherlands would be among the first wave of EMU members and that Finland's chances were also high. He did not comment on other countries' prospects for early membership of EMU.
